name: TPS61165DBVR
title: TPS61165: white LED boost driver, 3 V to 18 V input, 38 V open-LED protection, PWM and one-wire dimming
summary: A 1.2 MHz current-mode boost converter for driving a series string of white or high-brightness LEDs from a 3 V to 18 V supply, with a 40 V, 1.2 A internal switch. The string current is set by a sense resistor under a 200 mV feedback reference (2% accuracy). Brightness is set on the single CTRL pin, either by a PWM signal that scales the reference (so the LED current stays DC and silent) or by the EasyScale one-wire command interface, in 32 steps. It shuts down on an open string at 38 V, and offers soft start, undervoltage lockout and thermal shutdown. TPS61165DBVR is the 6-pin SOT-23 on a 3000-piece reel; a 2 mm × 2 mm WSON with exposed pad is also offered.

circuits.title: Typical application: three white LEDs from 5 V
circuits.description: Boost converter lighting a series string of three white LEDs from a 5 V input. The inductor and Schottky diode lift the string's anode voltage above the input; the string's current flows through Rset to ground, and the IC regulates the voltage across Rset (pin FB) to 200 mV, so 0.57 Ω gives about 350 mA. CTRL switches the converter on and off and takes the PWM or EasyScale dimming signal; the 220 nF capacitor on COMP compensates the loop. C1 bypasses the input, C2 smooths the output.
notes: The string current is marked 350 mA.

circuits.title: Three high-brightness LEDs with an external PWM dimming network
circuits.description: Same boost stage as the typical circuit, but dimmed by a low-frequency PWM signal outside the IC. The PWM signal (1.8 V, 200 Hz) is averaged by 100 kΩ and 0.1 µF into a DC level, which 80 kΩ adds into the FB node; 10 kΩ joins FB to the top of Rset. A higher PWM duty cycle lifts FB and so lowers the voltage the loop leaves across Rset, reducing the LED current. CTRL is used only for on and off.
notes: LED current = 1.8 V × (1 − d) / (8 × Rset), d being the PWM duty cycle.

circuits.title: 27 LEDs in nine strings of three for a media display
circuits.description: Boost stage driving a 3s9p array: nine parallel strings of three white LEDs, 27 in all, from a 3 V to 6 V input. All nine strings share one return node, which sits on FB and on a 1.1 Ω Rset; the regulated 200 mV across Rset sets the total current of the array.
notes: LED11 to LED93: string s holds LEDs s1, s2, s3 from anode end to FB end.

circuits.title: Six high-brightness LEDs in series from 12 V
circuits.description: Boost stage from a 12 V input driving one string of six high-brightness white LEDs. Rset of 0.57 Ω under the 200 mV FB regulation sets about 350 mA through the string.
notes: The string current is marked 350 mA.

circuits.title: Four high-brightness LEDs with a SEPIC stage
circuits.description: SEPIC converter for an input of 9 V to 15 V, which spans the 12 V string voltage, so the output can sit above or below the input. L1 charges from VIN through the internal switch; the 1 µF coupling capacitor C4 carries the switch-node swing over to L2 and D1, and D1 feeds the four-LED string and C2. Rset of 1.1 Ω under the 200 mV FB regulation sets about 180 mA.
notes: The output is marked VOUT = 12 V and the string current 180 mA.
L1 and L2 may be one 1:1 coupled transformer instead of two inductors.

operation.text: A current-mode boost converter with a 40 V, 1.2 A integrated switch FET running at a fixed 1.2 MHz. The error amplifier output and the sensed switch current together set the duty cycle in a PWM comparator; a slope-compensation ramp is summed into the sensed current to keep the loop stable at duty cycles above 40%. The loop holds FB at a low 200 mV reference, which keeps the loss in the sense resistor small. A series string carries one current through every LED.

On enable the FB reference climbs to its target in 32 steps of 213 μs each, so the output rises slowly. For the first 5 ms after COMP starts to rise, the switch current limit is halved, which keeps the input current below 700 mA typical. Together these limit inrush.

Each switching cycle the IC watches SW and FB. If SW stays above VOVP and FB stays under half its regulation voltage for 8 clock cycles, the switch FET is turned off and the device shuts down; the output then falls to the input voltage. It stays off until CTRL is toggled. The string's maximum forward voltage plus 200 mV must stay under the 38 V minimum threshold.
Below about 2.2 V (typical) at VIN the device is shut down with the switch off. It starts again once VIN has risen by the UVLO hysteresis.
The device turns off when the junction passes 160°C typical and turns back on by itself after cooling by 15°C.

CTRL held low for more than 2.5 ms puts the device in shutdown, where it draws under 1 μA. The switch no longer runs, but a DC path from the input through the inductor and the Schottky diode to the LEDs remains, so the string's minimum forward voltage must exceed the maximum input voltage for the LEDs to stay dark.

Two dimming modes share the CTRL pin: PWM (the default) and EasyScale one-wire. The choice is made at every start from shutdown. To get EasyScale, take CTRL high to enable the part and open the 1 ms detection window; after the 100 μs detection delay, hold CTRL low for longer than the 260 μs detection time, all before the window closes (the window counts from the first low-to-high edge). The part then enters one-wire mode at once, and commands may begin before the window ends. To stay in PWM mode, never hold CTRL low for more than 160 μs during that time. Changing modes needs a shutdown (CTRL low for 2.5 ms) and a fresh start.

With CTRL steadily high, FB regulates to 200 mV. A PWM signal on CTRL chops the internal 200 mV reference at its duty cycle, and an internal low-pass filter turns the result into a DC reference for the error amplifier, so FB = duty × 200 mV. The LED current is therefore a dimmed DC level, not pulsed, which avoids audible noise from the output capacitor, and the result does not depend on the PWM signal's logic-high voltage. Use 6.5 kHz to 100 kHz; the lower limit follows from the EasyScale detection timing. CTRL is a logic input, so an RC filter on it does not work; for lower PWM frequencies an RC network on FB is used instead (the external-PWM circuit).

EasyScale sets FB to one of 32 steps in a single command; the steps grow with level for a roughly logarithmic brightness scale (selectable FB voltage table). At first enable the step is full scale, 200 mV. The chosen step is held in a register through a CTRL-low shutdown of 2.5 ms and re-enable; only a power reset returns it to the default. Each command is two bytes sent MSB first: the device address 72 hex, then a data byte holding RFA, address bits A1 and A0 (both 0) and five data bits D4 to D0. Bit rates from 1.7 kbit/s up to 160 kbit/s are detected automatically. No PWM signal has to run continuously, so the host processor can save power or go idle.

Before each byte the host gives a start condition, CTRL high for at least tstart (2 μs); if CTRL is already high, the address byte needs none. Each byte ends with an end-of-stream condition lasting at least tEOS (2 μs). A bit runs from one falling edge to the next: a logic 1 has its high time at least twice its low time, a logic 0 its low time at least twice its high time.

The device acknowledges only when RFA is set, the address matches and all 16 bits arrive intact. After tvalACK from the last falling edge it turns on an internal MOSFET that pulls CTRL low for up to 512 μs (tACKN). The host keeps the line low for tvalACK, then releases it and reads a 0 as the acknowledge; the line is free again once the acknowledge ends. Acknowledge needs an open-drain host with a pull-up. With a push-pull host, a series resistor in the CTRL line limiting current to 500 μA guards the internal MOSFET against an accidental acknowledge request.
A sense resistor Rset in series with the string, from its bottom end to ground, has its top on FB. The loop holds FB at 0.2 V (or the dimmed value), so ILED = VFB / RSET.

The switch current limit caps peak inductor current and so input power at a given input voltage. Output current available therefore depends on current limit, input and output voltage, efficiency, and the ripple, which is subtracted from the peak; the ripple depends on switching frequency, inductance and duty cycle.

Inductance, DC resistance and saturation current all matter. The part must carry the DC inductor current plus half the ripple without saturating; inductance can fall 20% to 35% near saturation and carries ±20% tolerance at zero bias. Too small an inductance pushes the converter into discontinuous mode, cutting output current and efficiency and raising input ripple. 10 μH to 22 μH is the recommended range, 22 μH giving the best efficiency in most designs with low ripple; the range already allows for −40% and +20% tolerance. Below 10 μH the built-in slope compensation may not suffice and the loop can go unstable, so other values need checking in the application.

The 1.2 MHz switching calls for a fast rectifier. Its average and peak current ratings must exceed the average output current and the peak inductor current, and its reverse breakdown must sit above the open-LED trip voltage. ONSemi MBR0540 and ZETEX ZHCS400 are the named parts.
C3, from COMP to ground, stabilizes the feedback loop; 220 nF ceramic suits most designs.

The output capacitor is chosen for ripple and loop stability. A ceramic capacitor's ESR ripple is negligible; with tantalum or electrolytic parts it counts. Ceramic capacitance drops with DC bias, ageing and AC signal: a 1206 part can self-resonate near the switching frequency, and up to 50% can be lost at rated voltage, so leave voltage margin. Use 1 μF to 4.7 μF at the input and 1 μF to 10 μF at the output; below that output range the loop may become unstable.

Raising VFB by EasyScale from 0 mV to any higher value can, in some units, skip soft start: with VFB under 10 mV the amplifier's input offset, larger than expected and of the opposite sign, may leave its output high, so the modulator turns fully on and SW and the output overshoot. An overshoot past the SW absolute maximum destroys the device. Do not step from 0 mV with EasyScale. Either start from VFB = 10 mV and step up, or shut down with CTRL low for 2.5 ms and re-enter EasyScale so the part soft-starts from 0 mV to the default 200 mV.
One supply of 3 V to 18 V, able to deliver the input current the application draws.

SW switches fast to save loss, so its traces are the noisy node: keep their length and area small, and run a ground plane under the regulator. The loop through the internal switch, the Schottky diode and the output capacitor carries nanosecond current edges and must be as short as possible. Place the input capacitor close to both VIN and GND. TI's layout example places Rset and C3 beside FB and COMP, C1 by VIN, L1 and C2 by SW, with vias around the thermal pad.

Keep the junction at or below 125°C in normal operation, so dissipation must stay under PD(max). The WSON package's exposed pad improves heat flow; its RθJA depends heavily on board layout and on the pad connection. Solder the pad to analog ground with thermal vias beneath it (TI application report SLUA271).
An AEC-Q100 qualified automotive version is sold as TPS61165-Q1, a separate device from the TPS61165.
ESD protection on chip is limited. Store and handle with the leads shorted or in conductive foam.
